utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, very much, Madam Registrar. I did understand, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that Ms. Pilipovic will not be attending the session of this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. My co-colleague is not here today. She asked me to tell you, to all of you, since we will not see each other again before next week, to express her sincere wishes for the upcoming holidays as far as she's concerned and all the best to all of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Ierace, I think the first thing we have to do is listen to you to whatever observations you might make to the request to grant a certificate for an interlocutory appeal in respect of the decision we have taken on the admissibility of the written statements of deceased witnesses. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, there is a tension between Rule 72(B) and (C). Rule 73(B) states that the decisions are without interlocutory appeal. (C) then allows for the issue of a certificate to appeal in certain circumstances. Those circumstances are, quoting the words of the Rule, where the decision "is appropriate for the continuation of the trial." Mr. President, it seems to the Prosecution that one may draw from those words and from Rule 73(B) that it is only in exceptional circumstances that a certificate would issue. In my respectful submission, those exceptional circumstances would apply where the Trial Chamber itself is troubled by the decision, perhaps, for instance, because of a conflict between the decision it is handing down and other decisions handed down by other Trial Chambers, in other words, where the Trial Chamber feels a need for an issue to be resolved at the appellate level. Secondly, in particular having regard to the words of 73(C), it seems to the Prosecution that there must be an issue which strikes significantly at the continuation of the trial. In other words, the ramifications of the decision must be fundamental to the trial. In my respectful submission, neither of those two concerns are made out in this case because the Trial Chamber has not found any conflict in the law in its judgment and, indeed, the request by the Defence recites that the law as found by Your Honours is consistent with that which emerged in a recent decision in the Milosevic case. The issue in the mind of the Defence is rather the manner in which the law has been applied to the particular circumstances of the statements of the two deceased. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is there any need to respond to the observations of Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, but only very briefly and only as regards to the form, if you will allow me. Thank you. I think that this Rule 73 is a problematical one indeed. It gives to your Chamber the authority to, in a certain sense, pronounce judgments on itself. It is something that we sometimes refer to as the competence regarding the competence, that is, the authority to decide on its own decisions. Subparagraph (C) functions in a way as a "lex specialis" with respect to the overall rule. We are here concerned with the administration of evidence and we have to examine the issue in light of these provisions. Let me tell you what our position is. What will happen tomorrow if the Prosecution shows these documents and then submits them to other witnesses or shows them in the context of a different procedure, a different investigation, and later on we come to a conclusion that it should not have been accepted within the framework of Rule 73? There is a logical necessity when it comes to the application of justice. We have to decide on this issue as soon as possible, or at the end of the trial, but then we will be faced with certain risks because a posteriori we will have to take the issue again. I don't believe that that was the intention of the author of the Rules. I think we have to be as specific as it is possible. We are trying to help you with these Rules, Rule 73(B) and (C), and I think that it is up to another Chamber to issue such a certificate so that the issue can be ruled upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. The Chamber will decide either today or tomorrow whether a certificate will be granted or not. May I remind the Defence that if a certificate would be granted, that although we are not sitting next week, there is still the time limit of seven days to file an appeal within the seven days. So it is just -- I don't know what decision we will take, but it would be a waste of time if we would grant a certificate and if then the Defence would forget about seven days' time limit for filing an appeal. Of course, if they want to file an appeal. Having said this, you can expect our decision either today or tomorrow. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I briefly raise one other issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And that is the timetable. As I understand it at the moment, formally, the Prosecution is required to complete its case by early July. As I indicated to you on Monday morning, the Prosecution is presently engaged in a thorough review of its case, that is, the part that remains to be presented. And in two weeks' time from then, which will be Monday week, if it is convenient to the Trial Chamber, I will inform you of any ramifications of that. In the meantime, however, given that we are required by you to finish the case in early July and having regard to the requirements of Rule 94 bis, that is the Rule which sets down the steps which must be taken in relation to expert witnesses, if that deadline still applies, the Prosecution then comes under some pressure to present the reports of its various expert witnesses. I note that the last edition of the Chamber's -- Trial Chamber's timetables indicates that Trial Chamber II will hear Galic, the trial of Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic until the 2nd of August. Mr. Prosecutor -- Mr. President, I give you every assurance that we are doing everything we can to ensure that the remainder of the case is only essential evidence, and whilst I do not wish to preempt what I will say on Monday week, I would be very grateful if the Trial Chamber in the meantime could confirm that we have available to us the month of July, so as to enable us to secure the expert reports and their filing without, if I could call it this, without undue pressure. I note that under Rule 94 bis, the time that the Defence has to indicate its position in relation to expert reports may be reduced from 30 days, but it seems to me that it is prudent to work on the expectation that there will be allowed the full 30 days. The space of a week and-a-half at this stage is, in fact, quite critical in terms of obtaining the reports in final form and filing them. I would therefore be very grateful if we did have that latitude to not be called upon to file them in the next few week and also the latitude to leave the final decisions in relation to timetable until Monday week, but in the meantime, some indication that we have the benefit of that extra latitude. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will consider the matter, and unless there is at this moment some observation to be made by the Defence...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Since we are discussing the issue of time limits, could we perhaps ask the Prosecution to state finally when they will be able to provide us with the response to the issue of, if I may call them document erosions, that is the problems that we have had with the documents that are now part of the case file. I am referring to the deleted or erased portions of the text. It is very important, Mr. President, for the Defence to be able to know with respect of their cross-examination, how these manipulations happened, and why. Could the Prosecution perhaps be given some deadline to provide this response so that we are able to prepare ourselves for the witnesses to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is not a response just to the observations made by Mr. Ierace, but another issue raised by the Defence, but raised before as well, and it also relates to the time for the preparation of case presentation or cross-examination. We will consider the matter, and I hope that we are able to do it today since we are not sitting tomorrow, but otherwise there certainly will be a way of communication between perhaps the senior legal officer and the parties if we would not be able to give you an answer to your question during a court session today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just two matters very briefly. I referred to Trial Chamber II. Of course, I should have said Trial Chamber I. And secondly, by way of encouragement, I can indicate that we have so far eliminated some 40 witnesses from the witness list. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Since you spoke about the Galic case, I assumed that you were referring to this Chamber and not another Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: May I be excused, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is the Defence ready to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Hafizovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will be my pleasure, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please guide the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hafizovic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Hafizovic, the Defence will resume its cross-examination. May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you made yesterday. Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I think that we left off yesterday with the issue of the location of the headquarters of the local brigade. I am once again asking you this question: Do you know where these facilities were located?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I am able to answer that question. I am not familiar enough with the issue in order to be able to provide you with any specific information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: During the events which we are now discussing, did you at any point in time see soldiers gathering at specific locations?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I did. I was wounded. I was interested in my welfare, and as far as I remember, didn't notice any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly that throughout that period of time during the war in Sarajevo, where you lived during the relevant times, you never at any point in time see any groups of soldiers in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't go out very much because of the shooting. I don't know what exactly you mean when you say "groups of soldiers" or "gathering of soldiers."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You do not understand what I mean when I say "gathering," the gathering of soldiers, a group of soldiers gathered together at a given location?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure I can give you accurate information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, then. Could you perhaps approximate?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As far as I remember -- if you would give me a moment, perhaps I could remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, I will give you this moment. Do you want it now or later on? Shall we later on come back to the issue?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it would be better at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Can we have your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I noticed that you had some hesitations in answering because you are not quite sure that you could give full and proper information. Just tell us what you know about it. If it is not complete, if there is anything you say, "I am not quite sure," just tell us what you know about it and then we will hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I am able to provide accurate information regarding these issue and I am -- I don't feel okay giving this kind of information that I am not sure about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, on a photograph which was shown to you yesterday, you saw a parking area. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it not true, Witness, that during the relevant times during these events, this parking area was used by the military?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You never saw any gathering of soldiers or equipment or material on this parking area?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I lived there, I didn't notice any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am now going to show you a map, Witness, and I should like to ask you to indicate on this map in general terms the front lines. So you can perhaps concentrate yourself on this issue. At this point, I should like to discuss another issue, the third incident, the third time when you were wounded, when you were together with a group of young people, with a group of friends.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was with a couple of friends. I don't know exactly what you have in mind. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were you not with your girlfriend and other young people?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not the third time I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I was referring to the third incident. I don't know how my question has been interpreted. I apologise. So which of these incidents is this one, the first one, the second one or the third one?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to the incident when I was wounded in the head, that is my second wounding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Let us discuss the second incident. What was the distance between the place where you were and the front lines?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but it must have been around 50 metres, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you were shot from that spot, from the front line?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building in which I was, that is the spot where I was wounded, and then in the direction of the front lines. I don't know exactly where they were because I never actually went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, but is it your testimony that you were shot at from the enemy front line?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, we all know by now that you were wounded, but you told us that the fire was opened from the so-called Serb army, by the so-called Serb army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was that mortar fire?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it correct that you testified that you declared that the round in question was an 82 calibre -- millimetre shell?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you stated that you were shot at from the enemy lines?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So is it the same line as the one that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I was wounded by a mortar shell, and at the moment I got out of the building and into the street, I heard shouts coming from the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this answer, but this is not the answer to my question. In accordance -- with respect to your statement, was that a mortar shell which had been fired from the enemy lines; is that your testimony? Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that I had been wounded by an 82 millimetre shell. A part of it was found later on by some neighbours. I don't know exactly who. But the shell in question was manufacture -- was of Yugoslav manufacture.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know what the firing position was when you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So it was from Serbian lines?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly whether it was from Serbian lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, thank you for this answer. Were there any other persons who were wounded in this incident, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were other people with me, but they weren't wounded. We were in the flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when you were wounded, did you go to the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you receive a medical document after this incident?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us where this medical document is?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have enclosed it with all the other medical documents. It has been attached to the other medical documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you received this medical document, what the date of this medical document is?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 13th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you said that you had been wounded in the head. Could you show us where, please.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, but you would have to approach in order to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, it is not for me, it is for everyone in this courtroom. Could you just show us the area in which you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As beneath your hair, which you apparently still have, is that correct? For the sake of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, for the transcript, you may indicate where the witness pointed at, but a comment was included. The witness points at his forehead just after the -- after where his hair begins, to a place covered by his hair. It was in the middle of his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is quite right, and we could add that, from a distance, no scar is noticeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, in the other incident that you spoke to us about when you were wounded, I think in the knee --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you were again commenting. Mr. Hafizovic, is there a scar on that place? You don't have to show it to us, but is there a scar on the place you indicated which cannot be seen by us because it is covered by your hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a scar on my head which is very visible. If anyone wants to approach me and to see it, that is not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I want to turn back to the other incident when you were wounded in the knee. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us, remind us of the date of that incident?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just repeat that, when I was wounded which time, what did you say exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I was asking you whether you remembered the date of the incident when you were wounded in the knee and in the finger.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded on the 24th of October, 1992. I was wounded in the finger and the knee on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you have any medical documents which relate to this incident?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Have you provided the Prosecution with them?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Since we are speaking about these medical documents, yesterday, we saw a document which is a medical certificate and there is a handwritten text on it, three or four words to the right and the right upper hand corner of this document. Who wrote these words?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think my mother wrote that. I am not sure, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If you are not sure about that, is there anyone else you could think of?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My mother is psychologically a little unstable, you know. She has a bit of tension, you know. So I think that she wrote that. If necessary, I can explain this to you a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I don't think it is necessary, Witness, but thank you. Witness, you said that the street in which you lived at a certain time was shot at by a sniper. Do you remember saying this?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you ever see that sniper, because you mentioned one sniper?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am talking about the place that they shot at, so there was a sniper shooting down that street, not only on one occasion, but on several occasions and over the course of several days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I will interrupt you there. Did you, yourself, see it with your own eyes, the sniper?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him with my own eyes, but I could see which direction it was coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, We have understood that. But you didn't see him with your own eyes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, naturally, I wasn't even able to look out in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So, Witness, as a result, it is not possible for you to know whether this person was a civilian or a member of the military; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to the person who was shooting?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We are speaking about the same thing.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, I will be very precise: The sniper. That is to say, you were not able to know whether this person was a civilian or a member of the military; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, usually when someone shoots at you, you don't look in that direction. You try to pass through, if you have to, and to cross over as soon as possible so as to avoid danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to interrupt you there. But do you personally know whether this sniper was a member of the military or not, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So as a result, it is not possible for you to exclude the possibility that this person whom you have mentioned was a civilian?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the point is perfectly clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, I would now like to move on to another series of questions which concerns humanitarian aid. You lived in the area in question. Do you know whether it is true that the humanitarian aid was distributed every 15 days? Was that the usual rhythm? So was the aid, the humanitarian aid, distributed every 15 days?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it was exactly 15 days, well, I couldn't be very precise about that, but it was distributed during certain periods which we all knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. The rhythm that I have mentioned, did this appear to correspond to the situation you were familiar with, was it more or less 15 days, every 15 days?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depended on how much humanitarian aid the international community would send, and depending on this, that is when the aid would be distributed. So if there was more food, it would be distributed every 7 days, but if not, then every 15 days. We could put it like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that answer, Witness. Do you know since when this structure of distributing humanitarian aid, sir, when this distribution started in Dobrinja, in the Sarajevo area?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as the international forces started sending humanitarian aid. I don't know the exact date, though. So in certain areas because they weren't able to provide food everywhere. Not immediately, at least. It was more difficult to get food in Dobrinja for a certain time because they wouldn't let convoys enter Dobrinja. As soon as the convoys started entering Dobrinja, they started distributing the aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, apart from these problems concerning the delivery, the punctual delivery of this aid, would you agree with me that the humanitarian aid arrived during the same period during which the UNPROFOR forces intervened in Bosnia and, in particular, in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The humanitarian aid started, well, I wouldn't give you any precise information about that, so I wouldn't want to go into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that answer. Witness, you said that -- when you were speaking about the incident in which you were wounded in the right arm, you said that this occurred in the street where there was an army office. Do you remember speaking about that?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded in the right arm on two occasions, if you weren't aware of the fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was there an army office there on each occasion?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some kind of office, yes. Premises of some kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, very well. Since you know that there was a military office which was close to the site of the incident, could you tell us how far -- could you tell us what the distance was in terms of metres?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that it was in the building which was opposite my building and that it was a military facility, and that I was a civilian so I never entered military facilities. That was forbidden, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, excuse me for interrupting you. I understand that you want to give us a lot of information. But for the moment, my question concerns the distance, the distance up until what you have called a "military facility"; is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say a military building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Between these military offices and the place we are talking about, what was the distance separating these two places, if you can remember it, at least approximately?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even say "military office," but I know that those premises --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hafizovic, the question is, you referred to a building opposite to the building where you were living at that time and that there was a military facility in that building. What Mr. Piletta-Zanin wants to know is what is the distance between those two buildings. Could you give us an answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was about 15 metres from one building to the other, maybe 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your help, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, would you agree with me that this military place - it doesn't matter what we call it - but it was very close to the site, too, the place that we are talking about; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could say that it was very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, since it was close, perhaps even if you didn't go there, it was possible for you to see what was going on there. Is it true to say that this was possible? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that is true. I was a civilian and I wasn't really interested in military things. I was trying to save my life. I was wounded a lot and I just didn't want these things to happen. I would just -- wasn't interested in the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hafizovic, Mr. Piletta-Zanin would like to know what you know about the military facility, whether you had ever observed what happened there or whether you know anything about what happened there, that is the question. Because I hear that you are more or less starting debate with Mr. Piletta-Zanin, and we are interested to hear the facts. So whether it was possible or not, just tell us what you know about it, about the military facility: Whether you saw it from a distance, whether you heard it from someone else; what do you know about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew that those premises were in the building which was opposite my building and that these premises were formally used as a sort of shop, a small shop, before the war. That is what I heard from others. But I don't -- I really don't know what happened inside. I never entered that place. I have been asked some questions, but I don't know what is being referred to. If I am put a complete question, I shall answer it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just, just saying for example, if you would have seen people you consider to be military people going in there without arms and coming out with arms, then of course you do not know whether they are distributed there but that's at least what you then have observed. What we want to know is what made you believe that it was a military facility and what kind of facility was it? I mean, if it is a shop, you can't park vehicles there. But in shops, you can make sandwiches for the military, you can distribute arms, you can distribute uniforms, or whatever. What do you know it? That is the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that they would occasionally go in there, people wearing camouflage uniforms, and sometimes they would come out. Whether they took weapons in there or took weapons out of there, I really don't know. So I know that there was some movement, that there were people who would go in there and come out of there, but I don't remember anyone specifically going in with something or coming out with something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... going in or in groups or, if in groups, were these groups of 2 or 3, or 10, 20, or 100?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not in groups of 100, that is certain. And as far as these other figures are concerned, I can't remember. Perhaps two or three, but I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I understand that it is difficult to remember, but can you be certain that you never saw weapons with regard to this military situation, with regard to this military facility?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. I am going to show you a map now that you will recognise. I have it in colour for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Madam Registrar, I just want to be sure of the number. Can you help me with that. I think it is 103, but I am not certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that everyone has received a copy. We will put it on the ELMO now, if the usher would help us. Perhaps the other way around. I think that it would perhaps be necessary to put it a bit lower down. Could you show us this part which includes the airport? A little more. That is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you recognise the part of Sarajevo which is Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. We are going to give you a black felt tip in a minute. I hope that will be fine enough to enable you to write down certain things, if possible. Witness, first of all, if possible, I would like you to indicate to us, to the best of your recollection, the location of the front line to the south of Dobrinja, in the southern part of Dobrinja. Could you do this for us?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please just tell me where the south part of Dobrinja is?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I am talking about the south of Dobrinja, the south-east of Dobrinja, to be more precise -- the south-west, sorry, the south-west of Dobrinja, that is to say the part which is directly adjacent to the airport.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the airport?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I mark this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Use the pointer to indicate it first of all, please. Indicate it with the pointer, please.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So at the beginning there were at the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, show us where at the time of these events the front lines were located.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the event in which I was wounded?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If you want to take these as a points which could help you to locate things, very well. Witness, let's do this differently. They said that your grandmother's apartment was shot at by a tank; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, let's take this as a point of reference. At that time -- at that time, do you know where the front line was?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the Serbian forces controlled the airport and this road here by the airport, the castle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Would you like to take a pen, please, and mark this demarcation line, the front line? Take a felt tip, a black felt tip.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that time they shot at my grandmother's flat and when we had to leave it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Precisely, yes.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of the buildings are marked so I am not able to indicate to you which buildings these are. But I know that the road here is the one linking up Lukavica and Kula with Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, if this pen is not working, take another one. I don't know whether it is the pen or not. Witness, would you please trace once again the line which you were indicating and which is not visible on the screen? Will you please trace it once again?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And now, Witness, I should like to ask you to mark with a cross the spot where your grandmother's apartment was located, that is the apartment in which you were wounded in your knee and your finger.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names of the streets are not marked, so I cannot pinpoint the exact spot, but it should be here, approximately, in this area. Approximately here. Maybe if you have a map with exact locations, I will be able to show you exactly where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please just mark the area with the cross, the area where you think it happened. I don't have any other maps.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either here or here, but I think it is here at this spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please mark the area with a cross.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I am now talking about the incident where -- in which fire was opened from a tank, as you indicated.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You told us, Witness, that it was possible for you to see, from your apartment, the tanks which opened fire. Can you, therefore, tell us from which direction the shots had come? Without marking the map, just with the pointer, please.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kula is situated above the airport so I think the area in question should be here. This is the hill. From this direction here, because I don't see any markings such as Gavrica Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Would you please put the circle in the area where you think the shots had come from. Just encircle the area in question.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I cannot follow you for technical reasons, but I think that Mr. Usher could place the map on the ELMO so that we can see it. Could you please mark with the letter "T" the area in question so that we know that we are talking about a tank here?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. Would you now show us once again on this map the location of the incident in which you were wounded in the head, that is, in this first-floor apartment. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not on the first floor. You have to be more precise. I don't know which wounding you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I was -- I did perhaps say the first floor. My apologies. But I was thinking of the ground floor, actually. The incident in which you were wounded in the head. I think it is the only one in which you were wounded in the head.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you are quite right, your question was not accurate enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I thank you very much for correcting my question. As far as I can tell, your memory serves you well.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that many of the streets here are marked and their names indicated, however, quite a few names are missing. I think it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you mark the area with a triangle, please. Would you please put a triangle on this spot.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So this is the location in respect of which you stated that the front line was some 15 metres away?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that that is the location in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you tell us with respect of this location, that the front line actually went through the buildings?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will repeat the question. I think that you indicated that the front line consisted of residential buildings?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You asked me to indicate the area, and I think I indicated the direction of the fire. There were many such directions. If you are interested in the one which resulted in my wounding, I will be happy to indicate it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We will come to that, Witness. I just want you to tell me whether "yes" or "no," the front line consisted of residential buildings?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It went between buildings, as far as I know, along one of the streets between the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And, Witness, can you now indicate on this map the place of the incident in which you were wounded once again in the right arm.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded in my right arm on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am referring to the incident involving the distribution of humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this was the spot. Once again, we cannot see the name of the street on this map but I believe that this is the relevant area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and mark it with a circle, please.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very good, thank you. Where was the military facility located, the one that you mentioned a moment ago? Is that the building that we can see right across the street from the indicated spot?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please indicate the area with a dot? With a solid circle so that we can see the difference.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. When talking about the incident involving a tank, you told us that it was your opinion that you were deliberately targeted?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. The reason you said that was because you were able to see the tanks?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tanks appeared several times at this location and they were quite visible. It was possible to see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that in front of your apartment in the direction from which the fire was opened by this tank, that there was a block of flats?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were they there during the war?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me now move on to another line of questioning. Witness, did you ever hear mortar fire coming from the Dobrinja neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dobrinja was divided in two. I don't know which part you have in mind, the BH side or the Republika Srpska side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The BH side.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, I didn't ask you whether you saw it, I asked you whether you heard such fire.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. Witness, when you went to hospital following the incident involving distribution of humanitarian aid, you were driven there. You were driven to the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Once at the hospital, did you see any patients, any wounded persons, who could have been members of the military?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If you are not sure, am I right in understanding that it is possible that the wounded soldiers were there as well? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't have any such knowledge. I don't know whether there were any wounded soldiers in the hospital. So I cannot give you a precise answer. But anything is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Indeed. Can you confirm, Witness, that at the location where the humanitarian aid was distributed, that as far as the distribution of humanitarian aid is concerned, that that was the only shelling incident?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, I don't understand your question. Are you referring to any specific day?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No. I am speaking in general terms. I am afraid the question is not quite clear. Could you try and provide us with an answer in spite of that?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind and repeat the question once again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is whether you know of any shelling when the humanitarian aid was distributed, other weeks, perhaps even other years. That is what the question is about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure. I don't have any precise information about that. There were such cases, but I didn't hear about them. I know that there was an incident involving a water pump and when some people were wounded. I know also that there was an incident at the Markale market involving the humanitarian aid. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is whether at this very place where you observed the shelling while humanitarian aid was distributed, whether at that same spot you know of any other shelling on other days, other months, other years while the humanitarian aid was distributed there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you once again for your assistance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, let me now move on with another set of questions concerning the Territorial Defence. Have you heard about that? Are you familiar with Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it true that the members of the Territorial Defence, in particular at the beginning of the conflict, did not have a regular uniform?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I heard, I don't think they did. But they may have. At any rate, I am not sure. All I know is that they were not well organised at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you know if any civilians established any militia and obtained weapons? I am referring to individual residential areas, residential blocks. Did they organise themselves locally?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not heard of any such organisations, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, see any -- any civilian or any such person using these buildings for their protection?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you see any trenches?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no trenches at the beginning of the war, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not -- I did not follow the B/C/S translation. I didn't use the word "tranchees" but "retranches," but maybe it is not of any great importance. Did you see any military vehicles, any tanks in front of these buildings?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you explain to me what you meant?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I was referring to a platoon, actually, to a small group of people, two, three, four.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this. I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when you left, when you went into town, you never saw any people who were some kind of guards in front of the buildings?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may just ask through the Court if the question could be a little bit more precise. I have tried not to intervene but I am having difficulty following some of these questions: Which buildings, where, what part of town, the whole town. What are the questions asking precisely?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must say, Mr. Stamp, that the questioning started more precise. It was about whether people organised in residential blocks, and I think it is an interaction between the answers and the questions. So perhaps I should perhaps ask Mr. Piletta-Zanin to be a bit more precise and to ask the witness to tell us what he knows, even if the question does not indicate what residential block it was. But if you know anything about people standing guard, for example, in residential blocks in the neighbourhood where you lived, to tell us about it. So I am asking you to try to understand the question to the best of your possibilities, and at the same time, I would like to ask Mr. Piletta-Zanin to ask the questions as precise as to his possibilities. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do my best, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would the Witness please be so kind and respond to the question.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, speaking of the military and what we were able to see, there were soldiers, but that they were wearing civilian clothes or military clothes, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you, Witness. My question was very precise: Did you personally see groups of civilians organised with the purpose of defending certain block of flats in Dobrinja; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is perhaps not that precise, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. What Mr. Piletta-Zanin wants to know, whether you ever saw people that you would, for example, on the basis of their clothing, people that you would consider to be civilians - so not wearing specific military uniform or military equipment - standing guard and thus giving the impression that they were defending residential buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have seen some civilians carrying some weapons. Of course, I saw soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the question mainly was about civilians, those not recognisable as military people, whether they would be in the neighbourhood of residential blocks, giving you the impression that they are standing guard or defending these residential blocks. I am talking about civilians, people with a civilian appearance, whether armed or unarmed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe at the very beginning of the war, during those couple of days, maybe. I probably saw, at the beginning of the war, someone in civilian clothes, according to that description. What exactly they were wearing and what they were doing, I don't know, but, yes, I saw some people in civilian clothes. I don't know whether you can understand how it was. Nobody was prepared for the war and it is quite possible that a civilian should have come out of their house carrying a weapon. If the counsel has any specific dates in mind and if I can remember them, I will tell him, but I don't know why he keeps insisting on these things, and I am not sure and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hafizovic, if you would just tell us, could you tell us in the later stages of the conflict because you said, "I might have seen civilians in the beginning of the conflict." At the later stages, what would you then have seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you mean at the later stage in the war? Of course, people walked around in uniforms, the military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were they specifically defending or standing guard at residential buildings or would you see them going to, for example, the demarcation line, the front line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the area where I lived, I never noticed anyone guarding any building. It was not necessary to guard buildings. But it is possible that people passed by carrying weapons. It would have only been natural.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me move on to another subject, Witness. Yesterday, you testified about a young woman who was wounded in the head. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You also mentioned a soldier who was there; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A man wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, let us call him the man in the uniform. How was this person evacuated?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded. I went up to her --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am sorry, Witness. I am not asking about your wound. I am interested in the evacuation of this person. How was she pulled out? Did someone carry her? Was she taken by a car?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two of us pulled her out of that spot by holding her by her feet and her hands, and we put her in a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What kind of vehicle was it?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly what kind of vehicle it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was it a military or a civilian vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that it was a civilian vehicle but, frankly speaking, I was not paying much attention to the vehicle. I was interested in the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, but it could have been a well-known make of a car. Was it a Golf, maybe, do you know?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that we have to have a break at this point. I only have a few questions left. We may have take up more time, but I don't think so. I think that we are still within the framework.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you are still within the framework and unless your questions would not take more than a couple of minutes, we would first have the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] A little more, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To give you an indication, if we would have a break until 11.00. Any question later than 11.30 would go beyond.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. I will be within that limit of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 11.05 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With pleasure, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to continue with your examination, with your cross-examination, at the point where we left off just a minute ago. You were speaking about this young girl. Do you remember this incident?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you do remember it, here are the following precise questions: What is her name?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already so in my statement, I don't know her name. I didn't know her before that event and I didn't know her afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What is her first name?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the exact date of this incident? When did it happen?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember that date. There were many such incidents so that it just became normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Time is precious, Witness, so I will move on to another question. You don't know when this happened?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: To which hospital was this person taken?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't go there. Probably in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thanks a lot. Witness, as far as you know, was there a report which was written following this incident?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, shortly after these events, were you questioned about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time such cases weren't investigated. This was something that happened all the time, so I was not questioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you are telling me that as a rule, as a general rule, no investigations would be carried out after such incidents; is that what I have heard?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not even after the first time I was wounded or after the second time, there was no investigation that was carried out. Many things were happening at the time and that was not a priority. The priority was to protect people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Witness, I would like to know if you are aware of an agreement which was concluded on the 23rd of March, 1992, and which regarded the evacuation of Dobrinja, the evacuation of civilians for whom this was necessary. Are you aware of the existence of such an agreement?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can talk about myself. I tried to leave Dobrinja, the town, and the state itself, if it was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, Witness, if you know anything about this agreement, could you please tell me that you do, and if you don't, just say "no."

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I take myself as an example, I tried to leave the country, but I did not succeed in doing so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hafizovic, the question is whether you know anything about an agreement, that means a formal agreement. May I take it that it was an agreement between parties. Do you know anything about an agreement made on the evacuation of people living in Dobrinja? Not your own experience, but whether you are aware of the existence of such an agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I am not aware of such an agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I was going to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. correct that myself. Thank you a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you are not aware of this so let's move on to something else. If we are speaking about your personal experience, are you aware of a place that is called Sunce? I think that this is a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please. What is it about?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will repeat the question but I think that it was clear: Do you know a place that is called Sunce; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know a restaurant that is called Sunce?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I don't think there were any restaurants.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am not asking you whether there were restaurants which were open or not, I am asking you whether you know of a restaurant that was called Sunce?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of any kind of restaurant that was called Sunce.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know a restaurant which was called Stela?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know a place or a restaurant called Borsalino?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Barsolino is in Alipasino Polje. That was its real address before the war. It is in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you pinpoint this place on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we need the usher's assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please provide assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you point to this on the map. Have a look at the map on your right. Could you show us where the location of a Borsalino is?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two such places. One is in the town and the other one is in the place where I lived. Do you want me to indicate both places or just the one in my area?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Show us both areas -- show us both places, please.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. The next one, please.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that you have a map for this. I can't find it on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you indicate the area for the other one, the area for the second place?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This zone is not on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Could you please take a pen - the usher will provide you with one - and in Alipasino Polje mark with a capital "B" the place where the restaurant Borsalino was located.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please mark it with a "B."

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, does the name "Kazani" mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thanks a lot. I am going to move on to another series of questions. If you could have another look at the map. You said that when you were wounded on several occasions, you were taken to the Dobrinja hospital. Could you show us where the Dobrinja hospital is located? Could you do this, please? First of all with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in this area more or less, but it is not marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you take the same pen, please, and mark with a capital "H," mark this place with a capital "H."

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just wait a minute to enable me to find my bearings?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Take your time. Take your time. I could guide you, Witness. Isn't it towards the area where you can see a sign for the post office? Isn't it close to that area? Can you see an envelope, which stands for the post office? Wasn't it quite close to this place?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The post office which is still there today? I don't know if there was a post office there before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I don't know. I am just trying to guide you Witness. If you know where it is, mark it with an "H."

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is in this part, somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Mark it with an "H" then so that we can see it quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, when you went to the hospital in Dobrinja on several occasions, did you never see military emplacements very close by, places of a military character?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I was in a state of shock, and I was in the car; I was wounded, and I think that this is something that you should understand. I wasn't looking around me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, I understand you quite very well. But when you left the hospital, you were not in such a state of shock, for otherwise they would have kept you there. So when you left the hospital, did you never see military facilities close to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't give you a precise answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You don't remember very clearly. You are not certain. Very well then. I am going to move on to another line of questioning. Witness, you spoke to us a minute ago about the fact that your flat was deliberately shelled. It was a shot fired from a tank. When this happened, are you aware of any fighting being conducted in the area?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not in that area because if there had been any fighting, we wouldn't have taken the risk to go out on to the balcony to prepare food, so it was not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did this tank only fire one shell and that was directed at your flat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And the only reason was to destroy your apartment?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you think about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I don't know. Unfortunately, I wasn't there -- or, fortunately, I wasn't there, but I just want to know whether this took place on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They didn't fire again. There was only one shell. It didn't fire at that flat or in the surroundings of that flat after that first shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, can I ask you what your father did during the war?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably like many other adults, he was in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You say "probably." Does that mean you are not sure?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know whether he had a weapon on him?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My parents are divorced. I am not very close to my father so that -- although the situation was such as it was, the relations between my parents were not very good. My experience was not very positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you went to Dobrinja to visit your father. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... your question, Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My father, my grandmother and my grandmother.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether your father had a weapon. Do you know it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I lived with my grandmother and my grandfather. But whether he had a weapon, yes, probably he had a weapon. Not on him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mr. Hafizovic, to listen carefully to the questions and then to give answers. If there is any additional information, we would like to have, for example, how you would know that or where you were living at that time, I am certain that either Mr. Piletta-Zanin or the Bench or Mr. Stamp later on will ask you. So you say your father had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My father was in the army and every soldier in the army had a weapon, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he take it home or did he just use it when he was on service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see my father very often. I lived with my grandparents during the war. When I did see him, sometimes he had his weapon on him. When he left, he probably left with the weapon, but I don't know. In the flat, I didn't see it. I didn't have any contact with the weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What kind of weapon was it? Was it an AK; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not very good at weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was it a hand arm, was it an automatic rifle, a Kalasnikov?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I saw it on several occasions, that I saw a pistol on several occasions, if that is what you are interested in. I wasn't familiar with the type of rifles at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us where his barracks was located, since your father should have been in a barracks?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I never visited him in such places. I know that during the war he came under Dobrinja and later on, when everything had been organised, I noticed that he was in the annex of Vranic [phoen]. I think that he belonged to that area, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell me where this annex, and the name that you pronounced which I haven't remembered, could you indicate where it was on the map?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a barracks here in this area. I am not sure where exactly, but that is the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Is it near the two squares that we can see in Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From Alipasino Polje, it is about an hour on foot, let's say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you be a little bit precise with regard to the location of these barracks? And did you go there yourself?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians were not allowed to enter military facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, but after the war, you could have gone there to see where your father had done his military service. Did you go there after the war?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't enter the barracks but I know where it is located exactly, but it is difficult for me to pinpoint it on the map, but I know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
