utterances.text: But could you locate it on the map, please, and tell us which street it was in?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the street but there was a barracks there and it was surrounded by a fence. You couldn't pass through the fence. And the location of the barracks...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you indicate it as precisely as possible on the map?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you encircle it, please.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This street isn't on the map. The map is not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Please encircle it, sir.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And could you mark it with the capital letter "K" for barracks.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thanks a lot. Since we are dealing with the map, do you know where the -- where the atomic shelters in Dobrinja were located?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the entrances to the cellars were used, or if there were no cellars, then entrances would be used, and the safest places were between several walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will interrupt you. But do you know whether there were any specific atomic shelters in Dobrinja; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have never been to such places.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So you don't know?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have heard other people talking about these places, but I have never been to such shelters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. If you have never been there, it is not necessary to talk about this. During the war, did you go to school; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Which school did you go to?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These schools were improvised ones. There were several places which we went to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. These schools, the buildings where these schools were located, were they used for classes?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go to such a school during the period I spent in Dobrinja, and I know that there is a school there now which didn't exist before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, I have another two questions to ask you and then we will have finished. Do you know whether the school buildings were used by the army for certain purposes?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether there were any sniper units in the ranks of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Stamp, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that you delivered to OTP investigators copies of your medical certificate for the injuries which you suffered in October of 1992 and January of 1993; is that correct? You said that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In respect of the three occasions, yes, I have provided with all Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of these documents, three documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, I would like to tender to the witness a document marked P3367B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp. Do you have any copies for the -- yes, you are preparing them as I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you look at the first page of the document that you have and tell me if you see your signature at the bottom of the page or a copy of your signature at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you see your signature at the bottom of the second page in your own language?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you see your signature at the bottom of the third page? And this page is in your own language.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you look at the top of the first page and tell me do you see a date there?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What date is that?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 24th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could you look at the top of the third page and tell me if you see a date there?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And those were the dates of the injuries that you testified about?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And are these the documents which you handed to the OTP investigator, or may I put it this way: Are these copies of the document which you handed to the OTP investigator?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are, I think. I think that one document is missing that I also supplied. But these are the ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The document missing is a document in relation to your injury on the 4th of February, 1994; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that was the document you were shown yesterday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp, are you going to tender these documents in evidence? It is just a question. Or do you want to have them --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Entered into evidence, indeed, Mr. President. Well, perhaps the Defence would indicate whether or not there is a challenge as to the existence of these documents or what exactly their case is about in respect to these documents. Questions were asked about them so we have produced them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first ask a different question: Is there any dispute about the fact that the witness provided documents to the Prosecution? I mean, that, as far as I understood, was the question put to the witness by Mr. Piletta-Zanin. He wanted to know whether the witness provided these documents to the Prosecution. May I take it that these documents have been part of the disclosure. So what is there in dispute at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at this point in time, there is no issue. I am very happy to be in the possession of these documents, but if you will allow me very briefly to continue along the same line as Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if there is nothing in dispute, I mean, no one asked any question apart from whether these were medical documents related to certain moments. And is that in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, not at all, Mr. President. But these documents allow us to establish something very important concerning the credibility of the witness, if it is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The reason why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could have presented them to the witness and you could have asked him whatever questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but, Mr. President, perhaps, but I don't know what the response of the witness will be. You have seen for yourself that he has been quite difficult in answering questions which seem to be quite clear to me. Now Mr. Stamp is submitting these documents, which is fine with me, but will you please allow me to pose three questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there was any difficulty as far as the answers you obtained from the witness, you have noticed my approach. So you can't hide behind that. I will give you two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That will be more than enough. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, a moment ago I asked you whether you observed any military facilities in the vicinity of Dobrinja, and you said you did not because you were in a state of shock. Do you understand this, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question once again. I think I was not well concentrated. I am afraid I misunderstood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. President, I will go on with your permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You said that you were in a state of shock and you said that you did not see any military facility. I am repeating your words. Were you in a state of shock on the 24th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 28 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry the question was on the 28th of October, 1992 and witness said: "On the 28th?" Question: "Yes, on the 28th of October."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, whether the witness was at another moment in a state of shock is not directly related to the production of these documents. It is not a question which comes up. We have heard testimony and you have had all possibilities to question the witness about whether he was treated, when yes, when no, so that is not related to this document. You may ask questions about the documents but nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have in front of me a document whose translation reads as follows: That the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter is not able to follow the counsel at this speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Slow down, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] I will try to slow down immediately. [Interpretation] This document, Mr. President, shows that the witness went to have his wounds dressed on the 28th of October, 31st of October, 3rd of November, and the 11th of November, 1992, and also on the 6th of November. So he went, according to this document, on five various occasions to the hospital after this incident. When I asked him whether he was able to see or not military facilities in the vicinity, he said that he was in a state of shock.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now I want to know whether he was in a state of shock on the 28th of October, 31st of October, the 6th of November and the 11th of November.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hafizovic, you have answered all the questions by the parties, and since the Judges have no additional questions to you, this concludes your testimony in this Court. It is quite a distance; it must have been a quite new experience for you perhaps to appear in Court. We thank you very much for coming to The Hague and to answer all the questions because it is important for this Chamber to hear the answer of witnesses to questions of the parties. So thank you very much for coming, and you are excused for now. Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Hafizovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please guide us through the documents, and I would like to get a clear indication from the parties. One of the problems in respect of the last documents is that there are now full translations there. If it is just about dates, well, I don't think -- we have seen so many medical documents by now, that we see if there is a sequence of dates, this usually means that the patient has been on these dates and whatever way of treatment or control. I don't know whether it is really necessary because the question about the dates and whether he was in a state of shock could be put and answered also without using the document as such in evidence. If the parties would agree on that. But, if not, we will have to see how we will deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think it is clear that we already saw that this witness went to the hospital on several occasions, which is only logical. He obviously needed check-ups. He said that he didn't know about certain things because he was in a state of shock, and later on he said that he was not in a state of shock subsequently. As far as we are concerned, we can stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let's not confuse things. In my recollection, the testimony about the state of shock was not at a moment where his knee and his finger was wounded. He has testified about several occasions where he was wounded. He has been testifying about the other medical document, and that was a different treatment from the one on P3367B. So I want to know now from the parties whether it is in dispute that the witness has been in hospital in late October and early November, 1992, being treated on a wound on his knee and on his third finger of his right hand, and whether-- and that he was not in shock at this moment. Is that in dispute between the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is the evidence that the Prosecution tendered, then it is really a matter for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin are you contesting? Are you contesting --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then I think we can do without the document as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless anyone gives another good reason to have it admitted into evidence. Then, Madam Registrar, could you please further guide us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3367, specialist's report of 4 February, 1994 in B/C/S; P3367.1, English translation; P3232, map pre-marked by the witness; Exhibit P3678B, 360-degree Quicktime movie; Exhibit D102, map marked by witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All these documents are admitted into evidence and the Chamber is aware of the objections against the photograph. Mr. Stamp, is the Prosecution ready to call the next witness, which is presumably Sabahudin Ljusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Microphones are on in the interpretation booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Ljusa, I assume you are Mr. Ljusa. Before giving testimony in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of this declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher, and may I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Mr. Ljusa, you will first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you please begin by stating your name for the record?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Sabahudin Ljusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And what is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: The 17th of November, 1983.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you work now or not?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I am employed by a company in Sarajevo, and I am a car mechanic by profession.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you remember where you lived in February of 1994?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It was in Sarajevo in one of its neighbourhoods called Dobrinja. And the name of the street was Oslobodilaca Sarajeva, house number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, on the 5th of February -- I beg your pardon, on the 4th of February, 1994, were you injured in an incident?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, I am going to ask you to tell us slowly how you came to be injured, starting with a time, the approximate time when it happened. Can you remember the time it happened, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: It happened on the 4th of February, 1994. That day, humanitarian aid arrived which had been brought by a truck, which was then unloaded in a warehouse situated in a building in Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street, Dobrinja number X. I happened to be in the warehouse together with two friends of mine. Mr. Atif was there with us. I believe he was the president of the local community at the time. Flour was brought in some sacks but it was leaking and there was a lot of it on the floor. I think that Mr. Atif had gone to the location where this humanitarian aid is initially distributed prior to that. I believe that this location was in one of the apartments, at house number 9. I stayed there in the warehouse, together with these two friends of mine, and we needed a broom to sweep the flour off the floor and to clean the room. So Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I went to a building across the street, house number 9, to an apartment -- to the apartment where the humanitarian aid was distributed. This apartment was situated on the ground floor of that building and it consisted of two bedrooms. In one of the rooms, elementary school classes were organised, and the humanitarian aid was issued, distributed in the other room. I found a broom there. I took it and went back to house number 10, that is to a room adjacent to the entrance number 10. As I came out of the building number 9 and was getting near the building number 10, that is the warehouse, as I was crossing the street actually, some 5 metres before the actual road, I felt a very loud explosion and I realised that something had hit me in the chest. At that moment I wasn't aware of what was happening. All I could feel was a very sharp pain in my chest. I was thrown down onto the ground by the detonation, but I managed to get up. I looked under my jacket and I saw that I was bleeding from the chest, from the lungs, that is. So I realised that I had been wounded and I went to the out-patient clinic which was located in the vicinity on the same street. This clinic was located in a room next to the entrance number 10. There was another small room which was part of the clinic which was next house entrance number 7. On the way to the clinic, I remember that Mr. Atif was behind me. I think that he was also severely wounded. I went down the street walking towards the clinic, and as I was getting into the clinic, I saw a lady whose husband I think was holding in his -- holding her in his arms. Actually, he was helping her to the clinic. I also think that I saw a red dot on her forehead, which must have been blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you remember her name?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: She lived in the neighbourhood. I think that her name is Jadranka. So I went inside the clinic. There was a lot of panic there. There was an armchair which was not occupied and I sat down, and as far as I remember, I was not given help right away because the clinic was crowded with wounded people who were panicking. But after a while, I was given medical assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you take anywhere from there? Did you remain in the clinic or were you taken to another medical facility?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: This was just an out-patient clinic or an infirmary where first aid was administered. They treated my wound only initially there. They covered it. I was breathing with some difficulty, and after a short period of time, a vehicle arrived. I believe it was a private car. But I think that it had come from the Dobrinja hospital, because there was a hospital in Dobrinja neighbourhood, a wartime make-shift hospital, to which I was eventually taken in this car.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you treated there?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was given medical help there. It lasted a little longer than it did in the clinic. But again, I was admitted to that hospital only on a temporary basis, and since I was amongst the severely wounded, I was with a group of people who were waiting for a vehicle that would finally transport them to the Kosevo hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And were you eventually transported to the Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I got into a van which drove me to the Kosevo hospital where I was treated and where a surgery was performed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you remember how long you stayed in that hospital?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I think for about 18 or 20 days, but I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to take you back to the event on Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street. That is the name of the street; do I have it right?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At that time when this explosion occurred, did you see any soldiers or military personnel on the street?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers or military personnel there while the humanitarian aid was being unloaded?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That day humanitarian aid had arrived, were there people gathered or gathering around on this street?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember, there were quite a lot of people who were there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you said you were with two friends. How old were your two friends? Were they about your age, younger or older, or just approximate?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: They were of my age. I think that they both went to primary school with me. We were in the same class.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After you felt that explosion, do you recall hearing any other explosion?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I think I heard an explosion while I was in the out-patient clinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you recall where the sound of that explosion came from?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I don't know where it came from exactly. There was a lot of panic in the clinic, but I just heard this explosion. I couldn't say where it came from exactly, but there was an explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you know of any other casualties, or may I put it this way: When you said while you were in the clinic other casualties were arriving and there was panic, do you know where these other persons were coming from?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Well, not exactly, because I entered a room from which it is not possible to see which direction they were brought in from. But I think that it was all nearby because they all arrived at the clinic very quickly. Whoever could come on foot walked to the clinic. That was the easiest way to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall participating in a video production with an investigator of the OTP sometime last year, in September last year? Please answer verbally. Speak your answer.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ljusa, the interpreters should hear your voice in order to interpret what you say. They can't interpret if you are just nodding. That is the reason why.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in that video presentation, did you point out certain positions on Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, may I be permitted to show to the witness a video numbered P -- P3281D. That is P3281D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, leave is granted, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Could the video be played.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR: Could you please stand at the spot where, to the best of your recollection, you were located at the time the first shell exploded on the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]"

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you stop there, please. Could you move it for an instant and then stop. Please stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Behind you is the apartment from which you had taken the broom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that would be apartment number 9?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the position you are in now on this video where you were injured is the position you came out with the broom to cross the street to the room where the flour was kept; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I haven't understood the question very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The position you were in now is the position you were in when the shell exploded, as you said on the video?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And at that time, you were about to cross the road to go to the room where the flour was kept, to sweep it up?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you proceed with the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I will now mark this spot with yellow spray paint with the letter "X" and the number "1" on it. Could you please point to the location where humanitarian aid was being distributed on the day of 4th of February 1994. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Would you please walk to the location where to the best of your recollection the school, the mosque school, was located on the 4th of February 1994."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we proceed, could you tell us about this mosque school? Was there a mosque school being run in the community?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I don't know who ran it, but it was a religious facility. I think it was a religious, an Islamic facility, and children would go there to learn.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know if there were any children there when the explosion occurred on the 4th of February 1994?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I think that after I left the hospital, I found out that lessons had been given at that time and that there were children in that flat. That was a flat, too. But I think that they were on the other side, that is to say, in the other room which was facing in another direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you -- do you know if any of these children were injured at that time?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I think that they were wounded there, too, but not very seriously wounded. These are things that I found out after I had returned from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you please continue with the playing of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Will you please place your hand on the window of the apartment in which the mosque school was located. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: And now can you please indicate where, to the best of your recollection, the first shell exploded on the 4th of February 1994. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Will you please show me by walking to the location where, to the best of your recollection, the humanitarian aid was being stored when the first shell fell on the 4th of February 1994. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: And finally, finally, could you please walk to the spot on the street where the passageway begins."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we go into that part of the video, just tell us briefly about this passageway. Is it -- without leading, is there a way to get from the front or from Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street in the vicinity of where this explosion occurred and the park behind the apartments with numbers on that street? Do you understand what I am asking?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: You are referring to a passageway next to the park.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed. Will you tell us about that passageway.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes. There was a passageway in the building opposite the one we can see on the screen. On the other side of the road, there was a passageway. It was between house number 3 and 4. And it was possible to use this passageway to get to the park.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I just ask the technical crew to rewind slightly and we will proceed again. Thank you, we can start from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Finally, could you please walk on the spot to the street where the passageway begins. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Thank you very much for your assistance. I will now walk through the passageway."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thanks, we will stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You suffered injuries to your chest. Do you have any lingering conditions, medical conditions, as a result of that injury?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: It is not that serious. Everything is fine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you obtain medical papers from the Kosevo hospital after your release?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I received a letter of discharge from the hospital in Kosevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you gave copies of that letter of discharge to an OTP investigator last year?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President, But I would like to go back to line 15 on the present page. I think that I heard the witness reply in the past when asked a question by Mr. Stamp, I think that he said -- I don't think that he said it is not that serious, but that it wasn't that serious, and I think this is important because the witness was referring to his wound, and I think that this idea of the past is important. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are still waiting for the medical report so that might elucidate the issue anyhow. If that is true, Mr. Stamp, please proceed. If that is not true, would you please then clarify the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I take it when I asked you about the present situation with your medical condition, your answer is "It is not that serious. "It is not that serious, everything is fine now."

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes. I meant that it wasn't that serious now, but at that time when that happened, well, I wouldn't want this to happen to anyone. Not just that, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You told us that you spent about 18 to 20 days in hospital? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know how long exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So you really weren't saying that it wasn't that serious at the time, were you?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No. At that time, it was serious.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, may I proffer to the witness document P2252.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. And to the Court a copy of that document P2252.1, which is a translation thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you have a look at that document? And I mean to have a look at the four pages of the document that you have. Is that a copy of the document which you gave to our investigators last year?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said when you returned to your community after your stay in the hospital you discovered that some of the children in the school were injured. Did you learn anything else about any other persons who suffered as a result of this, who you knew at the time?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I think that there were quite a few such people, but I wouldn't mention their names. I am not sure who they were, what they were, but this was all in the surroundings. They were neighbours who lived in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ljusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I have nothing further in chief for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stamp. We are close to the moment where we usually have a break. So, therefore, I would rather first have the break before you will be cross-examined by counsel for the Defence, Mr. Ljusa. We will adjourn until 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 12.59 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will be my pleasure, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. You told us your date of birth. However, I should like to be sure and ask you to tell us once again the year of your birth.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Just the year?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, you can give me the month and the date as well.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I was born on the 17th of November, 1983.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember having given a written statement considering -- concerning the events that you have testified about?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I think I gave that statement to Bosnian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know when that was?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: It may have been in 1995, but I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, let us focus, if you please, on the incident which occurred and during which -- and in which you were wounded. How often was humanitarian aid distributed in your neighbourhood, at what intervals?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: At the time the humanitarian aid was not yet distributed. It started sometime after the arrival of the truck which brought the humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, I am sorry I have to interrupt you. I am not talking about the day when the incident happened. I am speaking in general terms. Do you know at what intervals, once a month, twice a month, twice a week, this humanitarian aid was distributed?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes. As far as this apartment is concerned in house number 9, bread was distributed, for example, every day. As for the humanitarian aid, I believe it was distributed every 7 or every 15 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, at the time you were taken to hospital for treatment, were you conscious?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: What hospital do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The one that you described as being a military hospital, the one at Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was conscious.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You have testified about this military hospital. Was it in any way different from any other hospitals such as a civilian hospital at Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, yes

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps it is my memory, but I don't know if my friend could point to the area of the transcript to where the witness testified about a military hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can try to locate it, if it's necessary, but the witness has spoken about a military hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just have a look on page 68 -- no, that is already in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 55, 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 55, line 6, reads that I am telling the witness that he will first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to see what it is. Maybe 58, 56 or 58. Let me check.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 58, 6, the testimony reads that: "I believe it was a private car, but I think that it had come from the Dobrinja hospital because there was a hospital in Dobrinja neighbourhood, a wartime make-shift hospital, to which I was eventually taken in this car." I do not see any "military hospital."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is possible that my recollection does not correspond to the transcript, but I am almost sure that this witness declared that it was a military hospital. I see him nodding his head. I can perhaps ask the question once again, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... check what the witness said before. But could you tell us when you were talking about a hospital, as it is in the transcript, a make-shift hospital, did you use the word "military" hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is possible that I have used this word because both soldiers and civilians were treated in such hospitals. Dobrinja was isolated from the rest of the town. As far as I remember, when I was admitted to this hospital, there were lots of civilians inside who were panicking. The situation was just terrible. And it was in this hospital that lightly wounded patients were treated there. Those seriously wounded were taken to Kosevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have called it a military hospital, is that because there were military patients or military staff, military doctors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. It was simply a hospital for everyone. Both soldiers and civilians were admitted to this hospital. And the doctors were, of course, civilians who worked in this hospital. But it was mostly civilians who were admitted to this hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, were there several hospitals in Dobrinja, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No. Only one, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So we are talking about one and the same hospital. Was this hospital close to the headquarters of a brigade which was located in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I don't know that there was a headquarters in the vicinity of this hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you see, in the vicinity of this hospital, any soldiers with weapons or groups of men in uniform?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, to your knowledge, with respect of this incident, how many people were killed? How many people died as a result of this incident?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Are you referring to the massacre in which I took part?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I wouldn't use the word "massacre," I am using the word "incident," but I am referring to that particular event.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Are you referring to what I personally experienced, to the event the way I went through it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You are quite right, Witness. How many people perished in this incident?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I told you about the lady whom I saw who had a bloodstain, I believe on her forehead, and the lady by the name of Jadranka. I remember that she got killed on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you personally know two individuals who were killed in this incident, and no one else?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I knew Miss Jadranka, who was killed. You are maybe referring to Mr. Atif. He was only seriously wounded. And I knew two more individuals who got killed in this incident, as I learned after the incident. That is, at the time when I went to the Kosevo hospital, I saw one of these two persons there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you personally knew three persons who perished in this incident?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No, only one in this specific incident, that is at the exact location where I was. But I knew two more individuals, two more persons who were killed on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, in total, you knew three persons who lost their lives on that day?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that there were three of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is quite confusing if you are asking about people you know who died or people you know of who died. You can know that someone died; you may even have seen it. And sometimes you do not know who this person is. I think that is part of the confusion that is both in questioning and answers not very clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President. I think I always emphasized "personally," that is, I was trying to find out whether the witness knew personally the individuals in question. But we will stick with the number of three.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you have a nickname, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not wish to create any confusion with my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. I didn't clearly hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My question is, sir, whether you have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I do have a nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: A namesake. I am not referring to a nickname.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: A homonym. I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know of anyone from your surroundings who has the same name and surname as you do?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Oh, now I understand you. No, no. There is no one by the same name and surname in my area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. And as we have seen and as you have indicated, you are now in a good state of health, so I take note of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could you help us distribute an exhibit, D103, which is a map. It is still the same map, Mr. President, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have another witness, you would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, we do not have a colour map for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you recognise part of Sarajevo on this map, in particular, the area of Dobrinja and Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, with the assistance of the usher, who will give you a pointer --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: -- can you indicate on the document which will appear on the screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the map should be placed on the ELMO, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you please indicate to your right-hand side, the map that is on your right-hand side, and indicate something for me. Do you recognise this map as being a partial map of the town of Sarajevo, including the neighbourhoods of Alipasino Polje and Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you think you can identify the location of the incident that we have been discussing?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: You mean the spot where I was wounded?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: The map is not very clear but I can perhaps indicate the general area approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please use the pointer to indicate this spot? No, no, on the map which is on your right side. I don't know whether the map can be zoomed in so that we can clearly see the portion in question. Witness, do you recognise the area?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: The map, I am afraid, is not very clear. I tried to locate the spot approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Could you just indicate the general area approximately where it was?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Well, I can try.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. You are now going to be given a pen, and would you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. please mark the spot with a cross.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It is actually a circle and not a cross, but it is all the same, after all. In this circle that you have just marked on the map, do you know whether there were any military facilities inside this circle? Just tell us "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I don't think I can respond to your question with just "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Because you don't know? If you don't know, just say so, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you think you could answer the question in a different way, not by just saying "yes" or "no," please give the answer you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that in this street, Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street, there was a not very large room which was used for the Territorial Defence, I believe, just for the purposes of the protection of the local residents of this street during the war events. So to call it a military facility, no, I don't think that it was a military facility of any importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was the distance between this spot and the spot where the accident occurred?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: As I said, it took place in a small room which was a kind of warehouse. This warehouse was located near the entrance at number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So what was the distance between the spot where the accident occurred and this other location?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe 100 metres or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this answer. To your knowledge, Witness, how far was this spot where the incident occurred from the front line?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: You mean from the separation line?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but that was further away. In the street where I lived at the time, there were only civilians who lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am sorry to interrupt you, Witness, but this was not my question. I have certain time limits. What was the distance, do you know, from this location and the separation line or the front line, if you know? If you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if there was a tunnel in the vicinity of this area?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You don't know or there was no such tunnel?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know if there was a restaurant called "Sunce" in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The same goes for the restaurant called "Stela"?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry, we couldn't hear counsel. Could the counsel repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Does the name of Kazani ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, let us go back to Dobrinja proper. Do you know where atomic shelters were located in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether the atomic shelters were used by the army?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: The shelter was not used by anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How can you be so sure?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Because I know that it was not adequate. It was simply not possible to use it as a shelter. The place was wet. There was a lot of water inside and it was completely neglected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Where exactly was this atomic shelter located? Can you indicate this on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I will try. I think that most of these shelters were located at various squares. As for my area, it was right above the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, but can you please indicate on the map what you know about the locations of these shelters.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there several such shelters?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: You mean where the shelters were?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No, there was only this one which was not used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Would you mark the area with the letter "A," the location which you just indicated.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I don't think I am able to give you the exact spot. I could perhaps encircle the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am asking you this, Witness, because of the time limits. If you can indicate it, please do so. If you cannot, just say so.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I am afraid the map is not clear enough for me to be able to indicate the exact spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness, but that is the only map that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just make a circle in the area where it was and then put an "A" in it so that we know approximately where it was.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Since you are familiar with the relevant events, can you indicate on this map the location of the separation line on -- towards to the south of Dobrinja, south-west of Dobrinja, actually?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No. No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If I tell you, sir, that the road that we see on the map and which separates the area of Dobrinja from the airport, can we agree that that was more or less the front line?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Are you referring to the road separating the airport from --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am thinking of the road which runs alongside this neighbourhood and which separates the area of the airport from the Dobrinja neighbourhood. It is the road which goes around the area of Bijelo Polje?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I don't think that the line was there

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interfere, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I indicated to you before that during cross-examination, if you touch new ground, so if you are not examining the witness on issues that have been part of the examination-in-chief, that usually leading questions would not be permitted, similarly as to an examination-in-chief. Usually, I do not mind that much if a leading question concerns something which is not in dispute at all. But you know and I know why a leading question on this very issue would not be the best way of getting the best information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will take that into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I would like to move on to another series of questions. Witness, was it possible for you to think that information that was provided after the incident in which you were wounded -- was it possible for you to think that this information concerning the number of persons who died was false? What do you think about this?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: You are referring to the incident that I mentioned in which one person --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. That is right. The one in which you were wounded.

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: When I said that I saw one person?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The incident in which you yourself were wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your question is about information, information provided by whom, to whom. What was the content of the information because there is nothing known --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will get to that. I am speaking about the information provided by the authorities about those who disappeared, who were killed. Mr. President, I am going to show a document to the witness. It will be a lot clearer. Mr. President, I am going to distribute a document which doesn't need to be translated, I don't think. The number is D104. And it is not necessary to translate it because it is a list of names and the witness will be able to read the heading of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you read the heading of this list? Could you read it to us, please?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: "List of people who died in Dobrinja on the 4th of February 1994."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, does this relate -- regard your incident?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please read what we can see under number eight?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Here it appears that I died in the incident. I don't know what I could say about this. This is so provocative, I simply don't know what to say. This document just is not clear. And I think that two of the names here are familiar. I know that these people died on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I can understand the fact that you are surprised because one doesn't discover that one is reportedly dead when one is in very good health. Could you read what you can see under number nine. Could you read what you see under number nine?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: "A child whose identity is not known."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, were you ever familiar with the identity of this child who is unknown?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I don't know who the person -- who the unidentified person is, but I know that one of the girls who had died on that day, I know who she was, but I can't see her name there. Perhaps they were thinking of her under number nine here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. Witness, you told us that you had spent this part of the war in Dobrinja. Did you go to school?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Where did you go to school, please?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: Well, in Dobrinja, we usually went to school in flats because in our schools, the conditions for giving education were not existent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether the school buildings were used for other purposes?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- could you tell us what the name of the school was to which you went before the war?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: The name of the school was Dusan Pajic Dasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I know that you were young at the time of these events, but do you know whether there were units or, rather, companies, whether there were mortar units or mortar companies in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I wasn't a soldier. I was just a child and I was only 11 years old at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I know that, Witness. Can I ask you another question: Was your father in the army?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were any members of your family in the army?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: No one from my family was in the army. My father was ill, so that no one was in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know whether the BH army had any snipers?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: One question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That document that you were just handed by counsel, do you know the origin of that document, where it came from?

utterances.speaker: SABAHUDIN LJUSA
utterances.text: I am not familiar with this document. I really don't know. It is very unclear. There is no stamp on it or anything. My first and last name is here. This is where they surprised me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. I have a question not to the witness, but you asked the witness where the document came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that there is an ERN number. Is there any explanation by the parties on what this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a document which we have in our possession which was disclosed to the Defence and which we expect to call evidence to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it is just to hear about the source of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed. It is just to demonstrate that perhaps with documents of this nature, there is no need to ask the witness questions about it. Because there is not much he could say about it. I think the Defence would know our --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It just tells us that there is a document on which is written that this witness died in the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says at this very moment. But we will hear more about the source of this document, that is what I understand from the Prosecution. So then I have no further questions. So you don't have to elaborate on that at this very moment. Mr. Ljusa, you have answered all the questions by both Prosecution and Defence. It is important for this Chamber to hear the answers to all those question given by those who have been present during the times and at the places which are part of this trial, so therefore, thank you very much for coming to The Hague. I know it is a long distance and you still have to travel back, but I wish you a good journey home again. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please lead the witness out of the courtroom. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you guide us through the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3281B, videotape; Exhibit P2252, medical documents in B/C/S; Exhibit P2252.1, English translation; Exhibit D103, map marked by witness; Exhibit D104, list of people who died in Dobrinja 4 February, 1994, in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All these documents are admitted into evidence. As I said yesterday, I hope that the way we proceeded during the last few days was an encouraging experience for both parties. Mr. Stamp, before adjourning, is there anything else you would like to bring to the attention of the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just quickly indicate to the Court that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Exhibit P3678B is an exhibit composed of more than what was shown in court, in that it was stopped -- before the entire video was played it was stopped at the part where -- I think I have the wrong exhibit number. Thanks very much. The exhibit number is P2381D. It was stopped at the part where the witness Ljusa completed what he had to show. On the next occasion when this Court sits, we expect to call the witnesses Hava Spahic and Faha Spahic that we propose to take the Court through the rest of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will see that at the occasion of one of the next witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, just to clarify something. I can see that they speak about -- its mentions the document P28. I am not sure that this is the document in question. This should perhaps be verified for the sake of the transcript. P28 appears on page 85, line 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see -- I take it that whatever confusion there might be at this very moment will be corrected. We know that it is about a videotape played today and on which the witness Ljusa testified, and there was only one video today. Is there anything else the parties would like to raise at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, perhaps just to repeat on behalf of Ms. Pilipovic, I would like to give -- she would like to give you her kind regards and tell you that she regrets being absent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that we will adjourn until the 6th of May. Madam Registrar, we are sitting in the morning hours, if I am well informed. That would mean that we will adjourn until the 6th of May at 9.00 in the morning, this same courtroom. And just as I wished everyone a good Easter weekend some weeks ago, I wish for those for whom Easter is still coming, a good Easter weekend as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
